text:
Maya R: Heads-up — p95 TTFT for chat-prod-default spiked right after yesterday's runtime push. Noticing impact on small sequences (<64). :eyes:

Samir: saw the spike on the alert. Which model variant? Any repro locally?

Maya R: gpt-small-legacy route, traffic ~30%. Spike start ~10:05 UTC.

PerfBot: perf job 19011 finished. Summary: baseline TTFT p95=200ms -> current runtime p95=450ms (+125%). Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/19011

Jon P: did infra roll anything overnight? kernel/driver/image updates?

Kai L: there was a cudnn minor bump on two GPU pools at 09:50 (8.9.x -> 8.10.x). Roll was staged.

Ashley C: checking dashboards. Also looking at batch-size distribution; short sequences suddenly show larger batch sizes.

Samir: can someone run a tight microbench breaking down TTFT and tok/s by seq len? I want p50/p95 per seq bucket.

Maya R: also we need consistent metric naming in dashboards; tickets use mixed terms.

Jon P: suggestion: standardize on "first_token_latency_ms" and "inference_tokens_per_second". Add batch_size_histogram.

Ashley C: agreed. I'll add panels and annotate the cudnn rollout time.

PerfBot: running: /bench --model=gpt-small-legacy --bench=ttft --seq-buckets=8,16,32,64 --runs=400

PerfBot: microbench results uploaded. Quick summary: seq=8 p95=520ms (baseline 180ms), seq=16 p95=470ms, seq=64 p95=220ms.

Samir: that's a clear regression for short sequences. Starting bisect between yesterday runtime commits and infra driver bump.

Maya R: for SLAs we committed p95 < 300ms for these paths — this will trigger concern.

Jon P: mitigation options: 1) routing small-seq traffic to low-latency pool (config), 2) rollback cudnn on affected nodes, 3) tune batching heuristic to prefer immediate dispatch for small seq.

Kai L: routing change is fast & reversible, I can prepare a config override. Batching tweak requires runtime restart on a subset.

Samir: preliminary bisect points to commit d4b2f9 (autoscaler batch-cut heuristic change) as potential culprit. Running focused bench with commit pinned.

Ashley C: I'll add an alert: chat_prod_ttft_p95 > 300ms for 10 minutes -> notify #eng-oncall and eng-runtime.

PerfBot: alert created: chat_prod_ttft_p95_sustained. Escalation configured.

Maya R: action list:
- Samir: finish bisect and post guilty commit + repro steps (ETA 18:00 UTC)
- Ashley C: add dashboard panels, annotate timeline (30m)
- Kai L: prepare routing override & batching patch (standby)
- Jon P: draft customer-facing blurb if SLA breach persists (>30m)

Samir: bisect update: isolated to autoscaler heuristic change d4b2f9 -> reproduces locally with microbench. POC: run bench with environment var AUTOSCALER_BATCH_CUTOFF=0.2 to mimic change.

Maya R: good find. If autoscaler is the cause, rolling that back is lower-risk than cudnn rollback.

Kai L: ok, I'll stage routing override to move chat-prod-default small-seq percentages to low-latency pool if we see continued breach. Won't flip until Samir confirms rollback commit.

Ashley C: dashboards updated: new panels for first_token_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99) + batch_size_histogram. Annotated cudnn roll and autoscaler merge times.

Product-team-bot: acknowledged. We'll pause non-essential experiments and watch customer dashboards.

Jon P: keep the incident short and async. If we hit 30m sustained breach, we'll post standard incident note.

Maya R: thanks. Samir please paste the bisect log here when ready and @-mention.

Samir: will do. Quick paste of repro command: `./bench --model=gpt-small-legacy --seq=16 --mode=ttft --runs=500 --env AUTOSCALER_BATCH_CUTOFF=0.2` — reproduces p95 ~480ms.

Maya R: perfect. Everyone on standby for Samir's final verdict. :thumbsup:
